A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–L support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material and reordered model-list entries.

before.justification: Sections 4–6 report original model-mapping analyses, benchmark-score prediction, empirical KL-divergence validation, and weight-interpolation experiments.

after.justification: The original empirical study is retained and extended with prediction controls, Mistral interpolation experiments, and estimated-versus-observed mean log-likelihood results.

M1.justification: Appendix J introduces an auxiliary procedure estimating merged-model log-likelihoods by interpolating source-model log-likelihoods, evaluated through their means. The main log-likelihood coordinates, double centering, distance calculation, and ridge-regression objective remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 10,000-text corpus with 17 categories, 1,018-model collection, 996-model prediction subset, and six benchmark tasks. The interpolation additions change model configurations and analyses within this coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds mean log-likelihood as an explicit performance-prediction reference in Table 3 and ridge regression using uncentered L as a comparison with Q in Table 9. V1's corresponding prediction experiment lacked these comparisons.

E3.justification: The main prediction evaluation changes from random five-fold splits to model-type-based GroupKFold splits. Appendix J also replaces 1,000 sampled interpolation-evaluation texts with all 10,000 texts and adds a Mistral base-model configuration alongside Llama-2.

E4.justification: New controls in Appendix K.3 test whether random splits inflate prediction accuracy and whether replacing centered Q with uncentered L matters. Appendix J extends the weight-grid analysis to Mistral and adds a direct test of estimating merged models' mean log-likelihoods through interpolation.

E5.justification: V1 already averages predictions over five seeded splits and reports correlation means and standard deviations in Table 6. V2 retains this reporting practice in Tables 7–9; the changed settings, additional comparisons, and numerical values do not introduce a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces the prediction results under the revised split protocol: 6-TaskMean Pearson/Spearman correlations change from 0.976/0.978 to 0.953/0.960, not a same-setting performance decline. V2 also reports new baseline and control results and interpolation correlations, including Pearson r=0.969 for Llama-2 and 0.973 for Mistral in Figure 20.

T1.justification: Appendix J adds the mathematical definition of the interpolated log-likelihood estimator in Equation 43. The central KL approximations, assumptions, coordinate identities, and proofs in Appendices B–F remain unchanged apart from equation numbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: scalable log-likelihood model representations, their relationship to KL divergence, mapping over 1,000 models, and predicting benchmark performance.

C2.justification: V2 explains the grouped-versus-random prediction difference through model-family leakage and interprets the L-versus-Q comparison as evidence that centered coordinates already encode performance information. It also proposes interpolation for efficient model exploration and updates the limitations to acknowledge related models carrying different type labels.

D1.justification: V2 adds a first-page code-and-data repository link, identifies GroupKFold as the splitting implementation, and documents enabling torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True) for interpolation experiments.

R1.justification: Related work adds Horwitz et al.'s model-atlas study and Zhuang et al.'s EmbedLLM. The perplexity discussion adds Liu et al. (2023a), Fang et al. (2025), and Thrush et al. (2025). These are focused additions rather than a substantial repositioning of the contribution.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and appendices A–L are retained. Local revisions expand Sections 5.3 and 6.3, extend Appendix J, add Appendix K.3, clarify terminology, and update author contact information.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 3, 8, and 9 and Figures 19–20. It also reformats nearest-neighbor tables and the dendrogram in bits per byte, adjusts map sizing and captions, and relocates several displays while retaining the overall presentation structure.

improvement.justification: Model-type grouping materially addresses v1's stated concern that closely related models could inflate benchmark-prediction accuracy. The grouped-versus-random controls and mean-likelihood/L-versus-Q comparisons substantially strengthen this central empirical application, while the code-and-data link improves reproducibility. Residual overlap across type labels remains acknowledged, and the new interpolation evidence supports mean likelihoods more directly than downstream task prediction.
